title: Serenity in Our Homeland (Kynjai Ha La Ri)
cultural_context: One of the crowning lyrical achievements of modern Khasi literature, from Soso Tham's Ka Duitara Ksiar (1936) and analyzed extensively in H.W. Sten's musical treatise. Expresses the tranquil joy, spiritual calm (kynjai), and unhurried freedom of living in one's own mountain homeland surrounded by murmuring pine groves and sacred rivers.
lyrics_khasi:
Kynjai ha la ri, ha la tnum ba pyngngad,
Ym don ba khuslai, ym don ba pynsalat;
Ki dieng kseh ki kynih ha ka erpyngngad,
Ka dohnud ka kmen ha ka suk ba kynjai.

Ki wahduid ki tuid da ka sur ba jemnud,
Ki mawsiang ki sngap ia ka parom mynhyndai;
Ha tnum u Lum Shillong ka lyer ka dang beh,
Ka nam jong ka Ri kan ym ju klet noh!

La ngi long kiba duk, kiba rit ha pyrthei,
Ha la ri ngi long kiba kmen bad shongkhrein;
U kba u la heh ha ki lyngkha ba iar,
U Duitara u tem ha ka sur ba phyrnai!
lyrics_english:
Serenity in our own land, beneath our cool highland roof,
No sorrow troubles us, no harsh distraction disturbs our peace;
The tall pine trees murmur in the refreshing mountain breeze,
The heart rejoices in unhurried, tranquil serenity.

The clear mountain brooks ripple with a gentle melody,
The ancient granite monoliths listen to legends of old;
Upon the ridge of Shillong Peak the breeze still blows soft,
The renown of our homeland shall never be forgotten!

Though we be humble and small in the eyes of the wide world,
In our native hills we dwell majestic and content;
The golden paddy stands tall across wide terraced fields,
And the golden Duitara plucks its shimmering melody!

stanzas.title: Ka Suk ba Kynjai (Peaceful Tranquility)
stanzas.khasi:
Kynjai ha la ri, ha la tnum ba pyngngad,
Ym don ba khuslai, ym don ba pynsalat;
Ki dieng kseh ki kynih ha ka erpyngngad,
Ka dohnud ka kmen ha ka suk ba kynjai.
stanzas.english: Serenity in our homeland, under cool roofs; no worries disturb us. Pine trees whisper in gentle breezes, the soul rejoices in tranquil peace.

stanzas.title: Ki Wahduid bad ki Mawsiang (Brooks and Monoliths)
stanzas.khasi:
Ki wahduid ki tuid da ka sur ba jemnud,
Ki mawsiang ki sngap ia ka parom mynhyndai;
Ha tnum u Lum Shillong ka lyer ka dang beh,
Ka nam jong ka Ri kan ym ju klet noh!
stanzas.english: Mountain streams ripple in tender melodies; stones listen to ancient legends. On Shillong Peak winds blow gentle; homeland honor never fades.

stanzas.title: Ka Jingkmen ha la Shnong (Joy in Native Soil)
stanzas.khasi:
La ngi long kiba duk, kiba rit ha pyrthei,
Ha la ri ngi long kiba kmen bad shongkhrein;
U kba u la heh ha ki lyngkha ba iar,
U Duitara u tem ha ka sur ba phyrnai!
stanzas.english: Though poor and humble before the world, in our land we dwell joyful and proud; paddy grows tall in wide fields, the Duitara resonates in bright tones!

vocabulary.kynjai: State of absolute peaceful serenity, tranquil leisure, unhurried ease
vocabulary.dieng kseh: Khasi highland pine (Pinus kesiya), iconic evergreen of Meghalaya
vocabulary.wahduid: Small murmuring mountain brook cascading over pebbles
vocabulary.mawsiang: Massive granite monolith or flat stone altar
vocabulary.shongkhrein: Dignified, majestic, holding oneself with self-respecting grace
vocabulary.parom: Ancient oral folklore, fable, or historical ancestral narrative
